name: Zero-width Unicode steg

technical_body.framing: U+200D (ZWJ) start marker + payload bits + U+200D end marker
technical_body.capacity_formula: 8 zero-width codepoints per payload byte + 2 delimiters
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible

notes: Renders as nothing in almost every UI. Survives most copy/paste, dies to Unicode normalization and to terminal glyph filtering. The default 'wants invisible' choice for text carriers.

name: Cyrillic homoglyph steg

technical_body.alphabet: Latin letters (a, e, o, p, c, ...) ↔ Cyrillic twins (а, е, о, р, с, ...)
technical_body.framing: 16-bit little-endian length prefix + payload bits, 1 bit per Latin carrier position
technical_body.stealth_class: prose-like
technical_body.normalization_risk: dies to NFKC — Cyrillic а normalizes to Latin a

notes: Plausible-prose carrier. Visually identical letters; can survive several thousand codepoints of prose covers. The go-to method when the delivered text must LOOK like normal writing.

name: CJK / fullwidth punctuation homoglyph steg

technical_body.framing: 16-bit LE length prefix + payload bits, 1 bit per ASCII punctuation carrier
technical_body.stealth_class: prose-like
technical_body.normalization_risk: dies to NFKC — fullwidth ， normalizes to ASCII ,

notes: Punctuation twin of cyrillic_homoglyph. Same story: plausible-looking prose, dies to NFKC. Handy for covers heavy on punctuation (dialogue, lists) rather than letters.

name: Trailing whitespace steg (SNOW-style)

technical_body.framing: 16-bit LE length prefix + 8 bits/line as trailing whitespace
technical_body.header_format: 16-bit LE length prefix distributed across first two lines
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible
technical_body.normalization_risk: dies to trailing-whitespace normalization (Slack paste, git config core.whitespace, most rich-text editors)

notes: Classic SNOW-style technique. Bytes-per-line encoding, survives raw-file transport, dies wherever the receiver's pipeline trims trailing spaces.

name: Invisible-ink Unicode tag block steg

technical_body.alphabet: U+E0020..U+E007E (ASCII-shadow: printable ASCII 0x20-0x7E mapped into the tag block)
technical_body.framing: U+E0000 start marker + ASCII-shadow payload + U+E007F cancel-tag end marker
technical_body.capacity_formula: 1 tag codepoint per payload byte + 2 delimiters
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible
technical_body.normalization_risk: dies to Slack paste (Slack drops tag chars from message body), some LLM tokenizer normalizers, but survives raw byte transports

notes: The technique behind the 2024 hidden-prompt-injection wave. Payload IS ASCII, mapped one-to-one into the tag block. Renders as nothing in almost every font/UI while remaining recoverable from raw bytes.

name: Variation-selector steg

technical_body.alphabet: presence of U+FE00 (VS-1) after an alphanumeric character = bit 1, absence = bit 0
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible

notes: Piggyback bit on any alphanumeric character. Renders as nothing when VS doesn't map to a defined variant. Survives most Unicode-preserving pipelines.

name: Combining-mark steg (CGJ)

technical_body.alphabet: U+034F COMBINING GRAPHEME JOINER after an alphabetic character = bit 1, absence = bit 0
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible
technical_body.normalization_risk: dies to NFC — combining sequences may reorder / collapse

notes: Similar shape to variation but uses a combining-mark codepoint. CGJ (U+034F) is defined to have no visual effect, so it renders as nothing.

name: Confusable whitespace steg

technical_body.alphabet: ASCII space + 3 whitespace variants (U+00A0, U+2009, U+202F) → 2 bits per space
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible

notes: Two bits per space by using confusable whitespace variants. Higher capacity than trailing whitespace at the cost of surviving fewer normalizers.

name: Directional-override steg (RLO/LRO/PDF)

technical_body.alphabet: RLO (U+202E) / LRO (U+202D) runs bracketed with PDF (U+202C)
technical_body.framing: 16-bit LE length prefix + RLO/LRO runs encoding bits
technical_body.capacity_formula: depends on cover — runs of paired directional overrides
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed

notes: Same primitive as the IDN homograph filename attack. Visible when it flips text direction; used here for a payload channel rather than an attack vector.

name: Hangul-filler steg

technical_body.alphabet: U+3164 HANGUL FILLER = bit 1, plain space = bit 0
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible

notes: Hangul filler renders as a blank slot in most fonts. Distinct codepoint from ASCII space, so parsers that split on U+0020 see a token boundary where the receiver sees payload.

name: Math-bold alphanumeric steg

technical_body.alphabet: Latin letter (bit 0) ↔ Mathematical Alphanumeric bold twin at U+1D400.. (bit 1)
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed
technical_body.normalization_risk: dies to NFKC — mathbold codepoints normalize to plain Latin

notes: Visible perturbation — some letters are noticeably bold. Trade stealth for typographic distinction. Python-only in this fork.

name: Braille-block steg

technical_body.alphabet: each payload byte → U+2800 + byte (256-codepoint Braille Patterns block)
technical_body.framing: no prefix — appended block after cover
technical_body.header_format: delimited by end of cover text
technical_body.prefix_scheme: none — payload as an appended block
technical_body.capacity_formula: 1 Braille codepoint per payload byte, unbounded
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed

notes: Every payload byte maps 1:1 into a Braille codepoint. The stego is visibly a block of Braille dots after the cover; not stealthy, but bulletproof round-trip through any UTF-8 pipe.

name: Emoji-substitution steg (🔴/🔵)

technical_body.framing: 16-bit LE length prefix + payload bits as red/blue emoji block appended after cover
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed

notes: One bit per emoji using a red/blue circle pair. Overt — nobody thinks a wall of 🔴🔵🔴🔵 is random — but round-trips everywhere emoji do.

name: Emoji skintone-modifier steg

technical_body.alphabet: 4 skin-tone modifiers (U+1F3FB..U+1F3FE) → 2 bits per human-emoji carrier
technical_body.framing: no prefix — appended block after cover
technical_body.header_format: delimited by end of cover text
technical_body.stealth_class: prose-like
technical_body.normalization_risk: on Slack paste, the modifier bits ride inside `blocks[]`; consumers that read `.text` get `:colon_form:` with the modifiers lost

notes: Two bits per emoji via skin-tone selection. Subtler than 🔴/🔵 — a run of thumbs-ups with varied skin tones reads as a real message. Slack-paste consumer must walk the blocks tree.

name: Emoji tag-sequence steg (black-flag payload)

technical_body.code_module: n/a (Unicode-level, composed via text_core.encode_invisible_ink over a black-flag base)
technical_body.alphabet: Base emoji (🏴 U+1F3F4) + U+E0020..U+E007E ASCII-shadow tag chars + U+E007F cancel-tag
technical_body.framing: base emoji + payload tag chars + cancel-tag terminator
technical_body.capacity_formula: 1 tag codepoint per payload byte + base + cancel-tag
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible
technical_body.normalization_risk: dies on Slack paste (tag chars stripped from message body), survives Slack snippet

notes: Legitimate Unicode use is subdivision flags (gbeng, gbsct, gbwls). Payload-carrying use hides arbitrary ASCII behind a single visible black flag.

name: Word-initial capitalization steg

technical_body.stealth_class: prose-like

notes: The prose-shape method: pick which words start with a capital letter. Survives every text pipeline that preserves capitalization; Python-only in this fork.

name: LSB image steganography (ST3GG v3)

technical_body.channels: R | G | B | A | RG | RB | GB | RGB | RGBA
technical_body.strategy: sequential | interleaved | spread | randomized (with optional seed)
technical_body.header_format: ST3GG v3 (password-derived HMAC-SHA256 magic + 16-bit length prefix + optional deflate + optional AES-256-GCM)
technical_body.capacity_formula: W * H * bits_per_channel * len(channels) / 8 bytes, minus header/CRC overhead
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible (small payload) | visibly-perturbed (large payload)

notes: The canonical ST3GG hide. Blue-channel 1-bpc randomized is the stealth default because blue is weighted lowest in human luminance. Chi-square / RS / SPA all attack this technique — see detectors.json.

name: Pixel Value Differencing (PVD)

technical_body.capacity_formula: sum over adjacent pixel pairs of log2(range_width_i) bits
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible in low-edge regions, visibly-perturbed in high-edge regions

notes: Payload bits go into the difference between adjacent pixels, with larger ranges (edges) carrying more bits. Better statistical stealth than raw LSB against RS/SPA.

name: Generic JPEG DCT steg

technical_body.capacity_formula: ~1 bit per 64 pixels (per 8×8 DCT block AC coefficient)
technical_body.robustness: low | medium | high — higher robustness embeds in more resistant coefficient positions at lower capacity
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible

notes: Robust to JPEG re-quantization when the destination Q matches the source. The 'tuned only' JPEG cell that survived Slack corresponds to careful choice of embed positions.

name: F5 (JPEG matrix encoding)

technical_body.capacity_formula: |nonzero_AC_coefs| * k / (2^k - 1) bits with matrix encoding parameter k
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible

notes: Matrix encoding lets F5 hide a k-bit codeword by flipping at most one of 2^k-1 coefficients, minimizing the number of changes. Shrinkage handling deals with coefficients decremented to zero. Detectable by F5-signature scan; historically the JPEG-steg reference technique.

name: jsteg (LSB over nonzero DCT ACs)

technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed at statistical level (detectable by chi-square)

notes: Simplest JPEG steg: LSB replacement on nonzero AC coefficients. The chi-square attack was designed against this exact scheme; treat as historical / puzzle-adjacent, not stealth-grade.

name: PNG tEXt / zTXt / iTXt chunk injection

technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed against any chunk dumper

notes: Trivially detectable by pngcheck / zsteg / stegg_read_png_chunks, but extremely common in real-world CTFs. Slack strips these on upload; survives on GitHub, HTTP raw, email attachment.

name: PNG private chunk injection (e.g. stEg)

technical_body.naming_convention: 4-char chunk type, second letter lowercase to signal private (e.g. `stEg`)
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed against pngcheck, invisible to sanitizers that strip only named text chunks

notes: Passes through Slack's named-chunk stripper (as of 2026-07 probe). Fragile — Slack could tighten the strip-list — but the current best PNG-metadata channel for `slack_upload`.

name: Trailing bytes past IEND / EOI

technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed against any tool that reads to EOF

notes: Bytes past the container's end marker. Trivially detectable but easy to add. Slack strips PNG trailing bytes on upload; JPEG trailer bytes are destroyed by the re-encode.

name: File-format polyglot (PNG-in-ZIP, etc.)

technical_body.header_format: magic-byte overlap between the two parsers
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible to parsers that only recognize one format

notes: The PoC||GTFO canon. A file that parses as PNG for image tools and as ZIP for archive tools, or PDF+ELF, or JPEG+PDF. Ange Albertini's catalog is the reference.

name: GIF comment-extension smuggling

technical_body.capacity_formula: sum of comment sub-block bodies (max 255 bytes per sub-block, unlimited sub-blocks)
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed to anything reading GIF comments

notes: The GIF89a comment extension. Byte-identical through most transports that preserve GIFs (Slack keeps GIFs byte-identical on upload).

name: GIF palette LSB steg

technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed at close inspection

notes: LSB over the global color table. Distinct from PNG LSB — the pixel data is palette-indexed, so tweaking the palette changes color, not pixel index.

name: APNG fdAT steg

technical_body.capacity_formula: sum of fdAT frame data sizes
technical_body.header_format: fdAT chunk grammar (sequence number + frame image data)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible to viewers that don't parse APNG

notes: APNG animation frame data as a payload channel. Static-PNG viewers only render IDAT; the fdAT chunks pass through unnoticed.

name: Matryoshka recursive-nesting steg (SPECTER)

technical_body.capacity_formula: recursive — nth level capacity is (n-1)th cover LSB capacity minus per-level header
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible per level

notes: Payload in an image in an image in an image. Depth-11 tested in the repo's SPECTER example. Each level survives what a single LSB survives (Slack upload byte-identical).

name: PCM audio LSB steg

technical_body.capacity_formula: 1-3 bits per PCM sample × channel × sample_rate * duration
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible at 1 bpc, visibly-perturbed (audible hiss) at ≥3 bpc

notes: PCM WAV / AIFF LSB. Survives byte-identical audio transfers, dies to any lossy re-encode (MP3, AAC, Opus).

name: Network-layer covert channels

technical_body.stealth_class: varies by method — timing is stealthiest, ICMP_PAYLOAD loudest

notes: Umbrella record covering every StegoMethod in network_core. Per-method detail lives in the network-* rows below; per-transport behavior lives in survival.json.

name: IP TTL field covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: IPv4 TTL (8 bits per packet)
technical_body.capacity_formula: 1 byte per packet — payload spread across TTLs
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible per packet (TTL varies naturally); statistically obvious in bulk (real TTL clusters at 64/128/255)

notes: One byte per packet. Real-world TTL distributions cluster tightly at OS defaults (64 Linux, 128 Windows, 255 BSD/router); a uniform spread across [0..255] is the fingerprint.

name: IP identification field covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: IPv4 IP ID (16 bits per packet)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible per packet (IP ID is host-chosen and often random on modern OSes); statistically obvious when strictly monotonic entropy appears in a supposedly-random stream

notes: Two bytes per packet in the IP identification field. Historically monotonic on old stacks; modern Linux/Windows randomize it, so a covert stream can blend in — until a statistical test notices the payload's non-uniform entropy.

name: TCP initial-sequence-number covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: TCP ISN (32 bits per SYN)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible if ISN entropy matches host (modern stacks use RFC 6528 hash-based ISNs — high entropy)

notes: 4 bytes per SYN. Only works on TCP handshake initiators. Statistically obvious if the receiver notices the ISN is not a valid RFC 6528 hash of (src, dst, ports, secret).

name: TCP timestamp option covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: TCP Timestamp Option TSval (32 bits per packet)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible if TSval delta plausibly matches host clock rate (typically 1000 ticks/sec)

notes: Overwrites the TCP timestamp option's TSval. Detection notices timestamps that don't advance monotonically with wall-clock or that fail the sender's clock-rate profile.

name: TCP window field covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: TCP Window Size (16 bits per packet)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible in isolation; statistically obvious in bulk (real windows advertise a handful of MSS-multiple values, not the full 16-bit range)

notes: Encodes payload into the advertised window size. Real hosts use a small set of window scales; a wide spread is the fingerprint. Also interferes with congestion control if used on real connections.

name: TCP urgent pointer covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: TCP Urgent Pointer (16 bits per packet with URG flag)
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed — real traffic almost never sets URG=1; every payload packet is suspicious on its own

notes: URG=1 with non-zero urgent pointer is vanishingly rare in real traffic. Anyone running Suricata / Zeek / plain packet counts notices immediately. Include for completeness, not stealth.

name: ICMP echo payload covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: ICMP Echo Request/Reply payload (variable, ~32 B/pkt in this impl)
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed — the LOKI2 lineage means every DFIR toolkit checks ICMP payload entropy

notes: The classic Loki/Loki2 channel. Highest per-packet capacity of the network methods and lowest stealth — ICMP payload with high-entropy bytes rings every alarm. Blocked by most enterprise egress filters.

name: DNS QNAME label covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: DNS QNAME labels (base32-encoded)
technical_body.capacity_formula: ~48 raw bytes per QNAME (single-label 63-char limit / base32 blowup)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible in noisy DNS; obvious to any resolver watching for oversized / base32-shaped labels

notes: The iodine / dnscat2 lineage. Excellent for egress bypass because DNS is almost always allowed outbound. Modern DNS-anomaly detectors (Splunk / Zeek dns.log) flag long labels and high-entropy strings.

name: DNS TXT record covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: DNS TXT record RDATA (base64)
technical_body.capacity_formula: up to 255 bytes per TXT string; multi-string records extend further
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible per response (TXT records legitimately carry SPF / DKIM / TXT-verification base64 blobs); statistically obvious in query volume

notes: TXT records are already a Swiss army knife (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, domain-verification). A covert stream blends unless the domain isn't expected to serve TXT.

name: HTTP custom-header covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: custom X-* HTTP headers (hex-encoded payload)
technical_body.capacity_formula: single-packet unlimited (bounded only by request/response header size limits)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible if the header name mimics a real vendor prefix (X-Request-Id, X-Amz-*, X-Datadog-*); obvious with unfamiliar X-* names

notes: Single-packet high-capacity smuggle inside custom HTTP headers. Proxies and WAFs sometimes strip unknown X-* headers; TLS-terminating egress inspects them.

name: Inter-packet timing covert channel

technical_body.wire_field: inter-packet delay
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible in the wire content; detected only by inter-arrival-time analysis (Cabuk/Brodley 2004 style)

notes: Bit rate depends on packet cadence, not link speed. Beats content-inspecting DPI entirely — nothing about the packet bytes is anomalous. Vulnerable to jitter-analysis detectors.

name: OutGuess (statistical-preserving JPEG steg)

technical_body.code_module: external — outguess CLI (not in this repo's img_core)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible against chi-square (that was the design goal); detectable by calibration-based / blockiness attacks

notes: First embedding pass hides the payload; second pass adjusts other coefficients to restore the original DCT histogram, neutering chi-square. Superseded academically by S-UNIWARD, but still the reference 'statistical-preserving' JPEG steg.

name: Echo hiding (audio)

technical_body.wire_field: single or paired echoes at short delay (~1 ms) with amplitude below perceptual threshold
technical_body.capacity_formula: 1 bit per audio segment (~500 ms segments typical)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible under casual listening; detectable by cepstral analysis

notes: Payload encoded as short delay between original and echo. Robust to modest amplification / bandpass; survives some lossy codecs at low bitrate cost. Not implemented in this repo; documented for completeness.

name: Phase coding (audio)

technical_body.wire_field: phase spectrum of the first audio segment
technical_body.capacity_formula: bits ≈ N_freq_bins / 2 for one anchor segment
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible (human ear insensitive to absolute phase); detectable via inter-segment phase-difference analysis

notes: Modifies the phase of the first audio block, then adjusts subsequent blocks to preserve relative phase. Perceptually inaudible; robust against small time-domain distortions. Not implemented in this repo.

name: Spread-spectrum audio steg

technical_body.wire_field: pseudo-random-noise (PRN) sequence added to cover at low amplitude
technical_body.header_format: PRN sequence known to both endpoints
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible unless the PRN is known; the go-to method for robust audio watermarking

notes: Audio analog of DSSS radio: payload times a PRN, added at low amplitude to the cover. Highest robustness of any audio-steg family; the historical basis for commercial watermarking. Requires shared PRN.

name: Spectrogram-domain image hiding (Aphex Twin style)

technical_body.wire_field: STFT magnitude spectrogram bins
technical_body.capacity_formula: one 'pixel' of the hidden image per (time_bin, freq_bin) cell
technical_body.header_format: image is visible when the spectrogram is rendered
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed once anyone opens a spectrogram viewer; invisible if only PCM samples are inspected

notes: The Aphex Twin trick (Windowlicker, ΔMi-1 = -αΣn=1NDi[n]). Draw a picture in the frequency domain, IFFT back to audio. A CTF staple; audible as a harsh chirp but visible in Sonic Visualiser / Audacity spectrogram.

name: Silence-interval steg (audio)

technical_body.wire_field: duration of silent gaps between spoken/audio segments
technical_body.capacity_formula: 1 bit per silent gap (quantized to short vs long)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible under casual listening; obvious if the same source is available for reference

notes: Encodes bits into the length of silences (short = 0, long = 1). Especially handy over telephone / VoIP where silence-suppression codecs are already re-timing gaps. Rare in modern practice.

name: MIDI SysEx steg

technical_body.wire_field: MIDI System Exclusive (0xF0 .. 0xF7) messages, 7-bit-per-byte payload
technical_body.capacity_formula: arbitrary — a SysEx can carry a full payload block
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible to normal MIDI playback (players ignore unknown SysEx); visible to a hex dump

notes: MIDI files carry System Exclusive messages that most players ignore. A canonical container-layer smuggle; requires a MIDI-file cover. Not implemented in this repo.

name: PDF post-%%EOF trailer bytes

technical_body.wire_field: bytes after the last %%EOF marker
technical_body.header_format: raw appended bytes; PDF readers scan for the LAST %%EOF and ignore trailing garbage
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed against pdfid / peepdf; invisible to normal readers

notes: PDFs terminate at %%EOF; readers seek from EOF backwards to find the last one. Anything after the final %%EOF is unreachable via normal parsing. Frequent in CTFs; strip with qpdf --linearize or pdftk output.

name: ZIP archive comment / slack space steg

technical_body.wire_field: ZIP archive-level comment (up to 65535 bytes) + inter-entry slack space + EOCD comment
technical_body.capacity_formula: up to 65 KB per comment + arbitrary slack
technical_body.stealth_class: visibly-perturbed against zipinfo / unzip -Z; invisible to `unzip file.zip`

notes: ZIP scans from END for the EOCD (End of Central Directory). Bytes between local file headers and the central directory, plus the archive-level comment, are unaddressed by normal extraction. Foundation of many polyglots.

name: SQLite unallocated-page / journal slack

technical_body.wire_field: unallocated pages in the SQLite freelist, rollback-journal / WAL leftover bytes
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible to SQL queries; visible to `strings` / any forensic tool that walks page structure

notes: SQLite databases keep deleted-row content on freelist pages until VACUUM. A steg author can pre-allocate pages, delete the rows, and leave the content behind for a receiver who reads the raw file.

name: compose_text_jailbreak (multi-technique composer)

technical_body.capacity_formula: sum of chosen component capacities minus per-component header
technical_body.header_format: per-component ST3GG framing; the composer picks a stack based on target model
technical_body.stealth_class: prose-like → invisible depending on component selection

notes: Composed pipeline that stacks text-layer techniques for prompt-injection payloads. See jailbreak_core.py for the template registry; each template names an ordered technique stack.

name: compose_unicode_tag_jailbreak

technical_body.capacity_formula: 1 tag codepoint per payload byte + framing
technical_body.header_format: start tag (U+E0000) + ASCII-shadow payload + cancel tag (U+E007F)
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible in raw text; increasingly filtered by 2025-2026 sanitizers

notes: The 2024 tag-injection attack packaged as a composer. Renders as nothing in a prompt but arrives as full ASCII to the model. Vendor mitigations landed through 2025-2026; test against each target.

name: compose_image_jailbreak (chunk + LSB + tag composer)

technical_body.capacity_formula: image LSB capacity + sum of chunk-body sizes
technical_body.header_format: ST3GG v3 for LSB, PNG chunk framing for chunk payload, tag framing for text-in-chunk
technical_body.stealth_class: invisible per component; visibly-perturbed to any tool that walks every layer

notes: Multi-layer image jailbreak: prompt-injection text in PNG chunks, cover image with LSB payload, filename with unicode-tag payload. See jailbreak_core.compose_image_jailbreak for the specific stack.
